title: Capital Markets and Investment Services Supervision
summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment firms, trading venues and issuers, from client conduct and client assets to algorithmic trading and market abuse.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to oversee investment firms and capital markets: assessing client conduct, execution and client asset protection, supervising trading venues and algorithmic trading, and detecting market abuse and misleading issuer disclosure.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a practical understanding of how investment firms serve clients and how securities markets trade, settle and disclose, together with the tools to assess whether conduct, controls and market integrity arrangements work in practice. Participants leave able to test firms' advice, execution and client asset arrangements, use surveillance and transaction data to identify abuse, and challenge venues and issuers with confidence.
sections.What It Covers: The investment services perimeter, investment firm authorisation and prudential oversight, suitability and product governance, best execution and order handling, client assets, trading venues and market infrastructure, algorithmic trading, market abuse surveillance and transaction reporting, issuer disclosure, and emerging risks in retail investing and tokenised markets.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for brokers, investment advisers, portfolio managers and other investment firms
Market surveillance, market infrastructure and issuer disclosure staff
Policy specialists, team leaders and heads of department responsible for securities markets
Learning Objectives: Explain the investment services perimeter and how capital markets are structured and regulated
Assess investment firms' governance, prudential resources and conduct of business arrangements
Evaluate best execution, order handling and client asset protection using firm evidence
Challenge trading venues, infrastructures and algorithmic traders on their risk controls
Apply surveillance and transaction data to detect and respond to market abuse
Design a risk-based supervisory approach to investment firms and markets, including emerging risks
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day workshops. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies, data and file review exercises and supervisory question sets, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's markets and firm population.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising investment firms or securities markets is helpful. No trading or quantitative background is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
IOSCO, Regulatory Issues Raised by Changes in Market Structure (2013)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)

modules.title: Investment Services, Capital Markets and the Perimeter
modules.summary: How capital markets raise and allocate capital, the investment services and activities that require authorisation, and how the IOSCO Objectives and Principles shape the supervisory framework.
objectives: Explain primary and secondary markets and the participants in each
Identify regulated investment services, activities and financial instruments
Relate the IOSCO Objectives and Principles to the authority's supervisory approach
syllabus: Market participants: issuers, investors, intermediaries, venues and infrastructures
Investment services: reception and execution, dealing, advice and portfolio management
Financial instruments, derivatives and perimeter judgements
IOSCO Objectives: investor protection, fair and efficient markets, systemic risk

modules.title: Authorising and Supervising Investment Firms
modules.summary: How the authority assesses investment firm applications and supervises firms on an ongoing basis, covering governance, fit and proper requirements, prudential resources and orderly wind-down.
objectives: Assess an investment firm application against authorisation criteria
Evaluate governance, compliance and risk management arrangements
Judge whether capital, liquidity and wind-down planning are adequate
syllabus: Authorisation: business model, people, systems and controls
Governance, fit and proper assessment and the compliance function
Prudential requirements for investment firms and the risk of harm to clients and markets
Wind-down planning and orderly exit

modules.title: Suitability, Appropriateness and Product Governance
modules.summary: How firms should understand their clients and products before advising, managing portfolios or selling complex instruments, and how supervisors test the quality of advice and distribution.
objectives: Explain suitability, appropriateness and client categorisation requirements
Assess the quality of advice files and portfolio management suitability reviews
Evaluate product governance, target market and conflicts in distribution
syllabus: Client categorisation and know-your-client information
File reviews: testing suitability reports and advice quality
Product governance: manufacturer and distributor obligations and target market
Conflicts of interest and inducements in advice and distribution

modules.title: Best Execution and Client Order Handling
modules.summary: What firms must do to obtain the best possible result for clients, how orders should be handled and allocated fairly, and how supervisors assess execution quality monitoring.
objectives: Explain best execution and client order handling obligations
Assess execution policies, venue selection and execution quality monitoring
Identify red flags such as payment for order flow and unfair allocation
syllabus: Execution factors, execution policies and venue selection
Order handling, aggregation and fair allocation
Execution quality monitoring and transaction cost analysis
Payment for order flow and other conflicts in order routing

modules.title: Client Assets and Client Money Protection
modules.summary: How investment firms must protect client money and custody assets, why failures usually surface only on insolvency, and how supervisors test segregation, reconciliation and recordkeeping.
objectives: Explain client money and custody asset protection requirements
Assess segregation, reconciliation and third-party custody arrangements
Evaluate the firm's readiness to return client assets on failure
syllabus: Segregation, trust status and acknowledgement letters
Daily reconciliations, shortfalls and breaches reporting
Title transfer collateral, securities lending and sub-custody chains
Case study: client asset shortfalls in an investment firm failure

modules.title: Trading Venues, Market Structure and Infrastructure
modules.summary: How regulated markets, multilateral and organised trading facilities and over-the-counter dealing differ, the transparency regime that supports price formation, and the supervision of central counterparties and securities depositories.
objectives: Distinguish venue types and their authorisation and rulebook requirements
Assess pre-trade and post-trade transparency and the use of waivers
Explain the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures and their supervisory application
syllabus: Regulated markets, multilateral platforms and dealing on own account
Transparency, dark trading and market fragmentation
Venue oversight: admission, rulebooks, surveillance and trading halts
Central counterparties, securities depositories and the PFMI

modules.title: Algorithmic and High-Frequency Trading
modules.summary: How algorithmic and high-frequency trading work, the risks they pose to orderly markets, and the controls, testing and governance supervisors should expect from firms and venues.
objectives: Explain algorithmic and high-frequency trading strategies and their market role
Assess pre-trade controls, kill-switches, testing and algorithm governance
Evaluate market-making obligations and venue-level safeguards
syllabus: Strategies: market making, arbitrage, execution algorithms and direct electronic access
Pre-trade risk limits, kill-switches and real-time monitoring
Algorithm inventories, testing, change management and annual self-assessment
Flash events, circuit breakers and volatility controls

modules.title: Market Abuse Surveillance and Transaction Reporting
modules.summary: How insider dealing and market manipulation are committed and detected, how firms and venues report suspicious activity, and how transaction reporting data supports surveillance and investigation.
objectives: Explain the main forms of insider dealing and market manipulation
Assess firms' surveillance systems and suspicious order and transaction reporting
Apply transaction reporting data to identify and escalate potential abuse
syllabus: Inside information, insider lists and disclosure delays
Manipulation typologies: spoofing, layering, ramping and cross-market abuse
Suspicious order and transaction reports: quality, volume and follow-up
Transaction reporting data quality and its use in surveillance

modules.title: Issuer Disclosure, Prospectuses and Ongoing Transparency
modules.summary: What issuers must disclose when offering or listing securities and on an ongoing basis, and how the authority reviews prospectuses, periodic reports and major shareholding notifications.
objectives: Explain prospectus and ongoing disclosure obligations for issuers
Assess the completeness and comprehensibility of a prospectus
Identify disclosure failures that signal misleading statements or abuse
syllabus: Public offers, admission to trading and prospectus exemptions
Prospectus review: risk factors, financial information and summaries
Periodic reporting, major holdings and ad hoc disclosure
Sustainability reporting and greenwashing in issuer disclosure

modules.title: Emerging Risks and Integrated Supervisory Practice
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining digital retail investing, social media promotion and tokenised securities, and building a risk-based supervisory plan for investment firms and markets.
objectives: Assess conduct risks from trading apps, gamification and online promotion
Explain how tokenisation and distributed ledgers affect trading and settlement
Produce a prioritised supervisory plan for investment firms and markets
syllabus: Trading apps, gamification and high-risk retail products
Finfluencers, unauthorised promotion and online scams
Tokenised securities and distributed ledger market infrastructure
Workshop: a risk-based supervisory plan for the sector

related.title: Supervising Financial Market Infrastructures
related.summary: An advanced ten-module programme equipping supervisors and overseers to apply the PFMI to trading venues, CCPs, CSDs, payment systems and trade repositories.

related.title: Agentic Finance for Supervisors
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to understand and supervise AI agents that transact and make financial decisions, from agent identity to payments and liability.

related.title: AI Governance for Supervisors
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess firms' AI governance, model and fairness risk, and to shape the authority's approach to AI supervision.

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.

related.title: Big Tech, Embedded Finance and Open Finance
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping supervisors to assess big tech, embedded finance and open finance models, and their concentration, conduct and operational risks.

related.title: Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals
related.summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving supervisors a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks they must supervise.
